Marcus / Olivia — attached is the draft spreadsheet with line-level answers. Highlights:

- Processing activities: generation, embeddings, reranking. For generation we capture prompt + response handling; for embeddings we note tokenization and vector storage behavior.
- Legal basis: Processing for performance of contract (API) and legitimate interests for platform improvement; we flag any customer-specific lawful basis to be confirmed in DPA.
- Data flows: Hosted API requests traverse our API gateway -> inference runtime -> ephemeral KV cache (per-request TTL) -> optional persistent logs (configurable). Diagram attached in cell A34.
- Retention: Default hosted logs = 30 days (configurable). Dedicated/Private: retention set by customer. We included how to request a retention exception for SOC/forensics.
- Controls: TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest for customer-managed disk volumes, role-based access control + audit logs; SOC2 Type II report attached as summary.

Open items (we marked with "ACTION REQUIRED"):
- Whether Nimbus requires a signed SCC addendum or will accept Redwood's standard SCCs template.
- Confirmation on whether Nimbus will consider pseudonymization for stored embeddings.

If you want a short walkthrough, I can jump on a 30-minute call.

Monica Patel
Security & Compliance Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
